§C.4 Ground Truth — Headings and Page Structure

What to do, when producing ground truth, in the cases the heading and page-structure rules leave to review. Each step serves the rule it links to; the rule decides the output.

Situation Step Rule
A page has a multi-line block (masthead, address, banner) Keep it as one block with plain newlines and flag the page, so it can be revisited when the open point closes Line Breaks Inside a Block§6.2
It is unclear which paragraph a marginal note annotates Keep the note as its own block near its printed position and flag the page Marginal Notes§6.4
A numbered line reads plausibly both as a heading and as a list item Apply the working default and flag the page Numbered Section Headings§6.5
A page is a table of contents or index Choose the form the litmus test gives, record the choice for the document, and flag the page so both encodings stay visible Table of Contents§6.10
A page is a transcript with numbered Q/A lines Apply the working default and flag the page Transcript Pages§6.11
Whether a page-top label is a running header depends on repetition on pages not in hand Check the surrounding pages; if they are unavailable, keep the label where the page prints it and flag the page Recognising Ambiguous Headings§6.7 · Recurring Page Furniture§4.6
Only one page is available and a heading's absolute depth depends on pages not in hand Keep the page's relative hierarchy and flag the page rather than guessing the level Recognising Ambiguous Headings§6.7 · Heading Depth Across Pages§4.5
